content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 toward a broken link without quoting the earlier-round sentence that pressed them or naming that round.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way.", "room": "A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way — reading 1: any verse counted toward a broken link needs the earlier-round quote and named round; reading 2: only a verse on the cited-in line being counted as an unanswered witness needs that, not the judge's own reasoning.", "why": "Because the rule requires a verse counted toward a broken link to be supported by a quoted earlier-round pressing sentence and named round, and the judge provides neither."}
